sentences: In a dark room, a group of people crowd around a round brass machine.
A light at its centre shines on the faces of children and adults alike, and every one of them is holding still, staring at the same spot.
This is A Philosopher Lecturing on the Orrery, by the English painter Joseph Wright.
It was first shown in London at the Society of Artists exhibition of 1766.
It is a large oil painting, more than two metres wide.
Wright was born in Derby, in the English Midlands, in 1734, and died there in 1797.
He began as a portrait painter, but at around thirty he started painting groups of people lit by a single flame, and these candlelight pictures made his name.
In London he became known simply as Wright of Derby.
The machine is an orrery, a mechanical model of the solar system.
Turn its handle and the planets move around the sun.
Here a small lamp has been placed where the sun should be, so the lecturer can show how shadows fall, and how eclipses happen.
Now look closely around the lamp.
One young man raises a hand to shield his eyes from the glare, while the young woman beside him stares without blinking.
Right beside the source of the light, each face reacts in its own way.
Look at the lecturer.
A grey-haired man stands behind the model, carrying on with his explanation.
His face, too, is lit from below, so he looks almost like an actor on a stage, holding his audience like a magician.
Then look at the children.
Two boys lean over the edge of the machine, their faces full of open wonder.
Nearby, a man standing up is busy taking notes on the lecture, quietly recording what he hears.
A single point of light in the darkness, with faces gathered around it.
Scenes of awe like this had long belonged mainly to religious painting, to miracles and holy events.
Wright put a science demonstration in that place instead.
For this reason, the painting is often seen as an emblem of the Enlightenment, the eighteenth-century age when science filled people with awe.
Two years later Wright produced another masterpiece of the same kind, An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump.
In 1884 the painting was bought by public subscription and presented to the museum in Derby, the artist's home town.
From the twenty-fourth of November until March next year, it is on loan to the Getty Center in Los Angeles, in an exhibition of Wright's candlelight paintings.
Step back and see it whole.
The people in the picture are not really looking at the light; they are understanding something because of it.
Today, why not look up one thing you have always wondered about, and give yourself a small moment of wonder?
